instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip (palms facing back).
2. Let your arms hang straight at your sides and keep your upper arms still.
3. Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping palms facing down.
4. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides.
2. Do not swing the weight or use momentum.
3. Keep your wrists firm and straight throughout.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward.
2. Let your arms hang straight at your sides and keep your upper arms still.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Pause and squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms close to your body and stationary.
2. Do not swing the dumbbells; move them under control.
3. Fully extend at the bottom for a complete range of motion.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip.
2. Let your right arm hang in front of your body and place your left hand on your hip.
3. Raise the dumbbell diagonally across your body toward your left shoulder, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Stop at shoulder height and pause briefly.
5. Lower the dumbbell slowly to the start, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced to resist rotation.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbow to protect the joint.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on your left foot with your right foot lifted off the floor, holding a dumbbell in one or both hands.
2. Keep your standing leg slightly bent and your torso upright.
3. Press through the ball of your left foot to raise your heel as high as possible.
4. Pause and squeeze your calf at the top.
5. Lower your heel under control to the start, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range of motion, lifting the heel as high as possible.
2. Do not bounce; move slowly and under control.
3. Hold a wall or rack for balance if needed.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in the calf.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell with both hands behind your head.
2. Bend your elbows so the dumbbell hangs behind your head, keeping upper arms close to your ears.
3. Extend your arms by pressing the dumbbell straight overhead.
4. Pause briefly at the top with arms straight.
5. Lower the dumbbell behind your head under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your ears.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso upright.
3. Move the dumbbell under control through a full range.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
